registered_method.rule: Treat each published dynamical model as a conditional history family. Preserve its priors, reservoir, sample size, controls, and failures. Never pool probabilities across incompatible models.
hard_constraints: measured present migration or dissipation where available
independent thermal, geological, and figure constraints

families.model_condition: Differential migration during satellite formation; larger Ganymede migrates first, captures Europa, then Io.
families.reported_outcome: The Laplace relation forms in about 100000 years and can evolve toward the present configuration after disc dispersal.
families.discriminant_status: not selected over later tidal capture by the present endpoint

families.model_condition: Measured present dissipation is continued backward through resonance encounters; chaotic branches and eccentricity damping are modelled.
families.reported_outcome: A later capture route remains dynamically viable, but the present lock does not uniquely select it.
families.discriminant_status: not selected over primordial disc capture by the present endpoint

families.model_condition: Single-resonance Hamiltonians, test-particle approximation, slow convergent migration, negligible relevant inclination/eccentricity damping.
families.reported_outcome: Capture probability about 6.0-6.6% for Mimas-Tethys and 100% for Titan-Hyperion.
families.discriminant_status: not a posterior probability for the real historical route

families.reservoir: tidal migration through a multi-resonance network
families.model_condition: Direct numerical integrations including three-body resonances omitted by two-body-only histories.
families.reported_outcome: Three-body captures are common and can persist for 10 million years or longer.

families.model_condition: Neptune begins near 24 AU; two-stage migration with tau1=10 or 30 Myr and tau2=30 or 100 Myr; 1000-4000 Pluto-mass perturbers or 1000 double-Pluto perturbers; 1000000 test particles per run.
families.reported_outcome: Twelve grainy and four smooth simulations show that graininess reduces resonant overpopulation and better reproduces the observed resonant/non-resonant ratio and libration-amplitude distribution.
families.discriminant_status: reservoir and migration direction selected; exact encounter sequence remains non-unique

families.model_condition: Four giant planets, 1500 primordial Pluto-class bodies, 4.5-Gyr integrations, multiple initial disc edges and primordial scattered-disc variants.
families.reported_outcome: Across 67 simulated systems, the best broad matches use a jumping Neptune, self-gravitating Plutos, and a 45-47 AU initial disc edge; detached and extreme populations remain underproduced.
families.present_status: independent current support with named failures
families.discriminant_status: strengthens the family but does not close all outer-system populations

families.reservoir: Jupiter-Saturn migration coupled to a planetesimal disc
families.history_class: sweeping mean-motion and nu6 secular resonances
families.model_condition: Exponential migration; initial offsets relative to current semimajor axes +0.2, -0.8, -3.0, and -7.0 AU for Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune in the published experiment.
families.reported_outcome: The model loses 62% of its pre-migration belt and reproduces excess depletion exterior to the 5:2, 7:3, and 2:1 gaps; total inferred migration-era depletion can be 90-95% but is speed-sensitive.
families.discriminant_status: selects sweeping migration over a uniform current-architecture erosion model; exact speed history remains model-dependent

families.system: Pluto-Charon and Styx, Nix, Kerberos, Hydra
families.reservoir: Charon-forming impact followed by Pluto-Charon tidal expansion
families.history_class: outward resonant transport of the small moons
families.model_condition: Multiple-resonance transport under constant-Q and frequency-dependent tidal histories, with Pluto figure and finite moon masses tested.
families.reported_outcome: No stable 3:1 or 4:1 transport; nonzero hydrostatic Pluto J2 destroys the required multiple-resonance condition; finite minimal Nix/Hydra masses yield no survivors.
families.present_status: falsified as a complete four-moon route
families.discriminant_status: constructive null: the boundary history is plausible but this transport mechanism does not reproduce the system
